task_retrieval_key:
A 29-year-old woman presented with hoarseness, dysphagia, vomiting, and headache. At age 31, her hoarseness worsened. No personal or family history of tuberous sclerosis was reported. Initial symptoms improved with anticoagulant therapy but later worsened.
Physical examination revealed paralysis of the right cranial nerves IX to XII (Collet-Sicard syndrome).

avoid: Do not treat an unsupported agent assertion as clinical evidence
recommended_check: Verify source binding before using the evidence for support or refute
